description: Five bounded legal time-rule records, with source-checked conditional civil-clock models. Research seed, not a geographical time atlas.
source_review: Official text and critical PDF pages read; interpretations and fixtures still require independent historical review before production.

encoding.calendar: proleptic Gregorian for these covered dates
encoding.reference_timestamp: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS, timezone deliberately absent; governed by each rule's GMT_civil_arithmetic scale
encoding.offset_sign: local civil label minus reference label, in seconds
encoding.interval_convention: offset_after is in force at the exact transition; before side is strictly less
encoding.unsupported: No leap seconds, fractional seconds, geographic lookup, record-calendar conversion, birth-time probabilities, UT1/TT conversion or current-law completeness.

rules.title: 1918 federal seasonal rule, conditional 75°W example
rules.applicability: Named legal regime only. No city, geographical boundary, birth-record or actual clock-observance inference is permitted.
rules.reference_time_note: Offset arithmetic only. Historical outputs are not physical UTC timestamps or UT1/TT conversions; no leap-second or subsecond claim.
rules.configured_standard_offset_basis: Conditional 75 degrees west meridian example; not a location assignment.
rules.interpretation: Section 3 advances legal standard time by one hour on March's last Sunday and retards it on October's last Sunday. Each 02:00 boundary is interpreted on the then-prevailing zone clock. Section 1 supplies the meridian; section 4 names the zone. Calendar dates are computed, not printed in the statute.
uncertainties: Zone boundaries require the relevant Interstate Commerce Commission orders.
The statute alone does not prove how an individual institution recorded a birth.
Only 1918 is covered here; repeal, local continuation and later years are outside this record.

rules.title: 1942 wartime advance, conditional 75°W example
rules.applicability: Named legal regime only. No city, geographical boundary, birth-record or actual clock-observance inference is permitted.
rules.reference_time_note: Offset arithmetic only. Historical outputs are not physical UTC timestamps or UT1/TT conversions; no leap-second or subsecond claim.
rules.configured_standard_offset_basis: Conditional 75 degrees west meridian example; not a location assignment.
rules.interpretation: The first paragraph advances legal standard time by one hour at 02:00 on the twentieth day after approval. Excluding the enactment day gives February 9. The before-clock is modelled as unadvanced standard time.
uncertainties: A locality already using an advanced clock may not undergo this assumed before-to-after transition.
No city observance evidence is supplied.
The original section 2 sunset is superseded for the 1945 end by the separately sourced 1945 record.

rules.title: 1945 wartime termination, conditional 75°W example
rules.applicability: Named legal regime only. No city, geographical boundary, birth-record or actual clock-observance inference is permitted.
rules.reference_time_note: Offset arithmetic only. Historical outputs are not physical UTC timestamps or UT1/TT conversions; no leap-second or subsecond claim.
rules.configured_standard_offset_basis: Conditional 75 degrees west meridian example; not a location assignment.
rules.interpretation: The 1945 Act explicitly overrides the 1942 termination provision and returns legal zone time to its meridian basis. The 02:00 label is interpreted on the then-prevailing advanced legal standard clock, producing a repeated hour.
uncertainties: This records the federal transition; subsequent local continuation or re-adoption of daylight time is not resolved.
A particular birth register may use a different stated convention.

rules.title: Uniform Time Act first general year, conditional 75°W example
rules.applicability: Named legal regime only. No city, geographical boundary, birth-record or actual clock-observance inference is permitted.
rules.reference_time_note: Offset arithmetic only. Historical outputs are not physical UTC timestamps or UT1/TT conversions; no leap-second or subsecond claim.
rules.configured_standard_offset_basis: Conditional 75 degrees west meridian example; not a location assignment.
rules.interpretation: Section 3(a) specifies April's and October's last Sundays at 02:00 and makes advanced time the legal standard during the interval. Section 6 gives April 1, 1967 as general commencement, with a separate conditional rule for places observing daylight time in 1966. The model assumes no state exemption.
uncertainties: The Act allows a whole-state exemption; applicability needs state-level evidence.
1966's conditional exception is documented but not encoded as a tested rule.
This record does not apply the 1967 recurrence to later years, emergency legislation or later amendments.

rules.title: UK summer-time order first year
rules.applicability: Named legal regime only. No city, geographical boundary, birth-record or actual clock-observance inference is permitted.
rules.reference_time_note: Offset arithmetic only. Historical outputs are not physical UTC timestamps or UT1/TT conversions; no leap-second or subsecond claim.
rules.configured_standard_offset_basis: GMT reference for the UK statutory model.
rules.interpretation: The Order takes effect March 11 and replaces the annual period with the last Sundays of March and October at 01:00 GMT. The Act supplies the one-hour advance. These transition times are in GMT, not the pre-transition local clock. Article 1(2) covers Great Britain and Northern Ireland.
uncertainties: Do not infer that dependencies or overseas territories share this rule.
Only 2002 is reviewed here; this file is not a current-law service.
Civil GMT offsets are encoded; no UT1-versus-UTC subsecond equivalence is asserted.
